## Natural history notes

A large ground beetle characterized by a metallic green body, reddish to coppery wing-cover margins, blue-purple highlights, long legs, and powerful jaws. In Florida, the Fiery Searcher is found in forests, hammocks, pine flatwoods, fields, gardens, parks, and wooded edges, often running on the ground or climbing tree trunks in search of prey. It is a beneficial predator, especially of caterpillars and other soft-bodied insects, and may also come to lights; when handled, it can release a strong-smelling defensive chemical.
